summary: Trickerion casts players as rival stage magicians racing to build the best magic show while sabotaging each other's supply chains through worker placement and card-based special abilities. It's a heavy, fiddly game with a lot of moving parts — action queue programming, dice-based effects, and a market that's frequently squeezed by competitors — that rewards efficient planning but punishes players who get boxed out of key spots.
praised: strong theme and gorgeous, characterful component design
deep worker-placement puzzle with meaningful blocking
satisfying variety between different illusionist characters
criticised: very long playtime and heavy rules overhead for the payoff
can feel mean when opponents block your planned actions late
top-heavy production makes it an intimidating table presence

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking and stealing resources
interaction.detail: Players compete for the same limited worker placement spots on a shared city board, and can bump, block, or outbid each other for locations and resources needed to stage their shows. Each player still develops their own tricks and reputation track privately, so the shared board is the main point of friction.

scoring.why: Fame is earned mainly by staging tricks well during shows, supplemented by reputation and end-game bonuses.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by staging the most impressive magic tricks during the show phases, built from ingredients and blueprints you've assembled through the week.
